hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Ali: They (the sandals) were made from the skin of a donkey, so it was said to him: 'Take them off.'

narrators.name: جابر بن يزيد
narrators.full_name: جابر بن يزيد بن الحارث الجعفي الكوفي
reliabilityIssues: Weak narrator, known for confusion, errors, and Shi'i tendencies

narrators.name: علي
narrators.full_name: علي بن أبي طالب بن عبد المطلب

chainIssues: Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi is a weak narrator (Da'if)
Multiple uses of 'an throughout the chain
This is mawquf - a statement attributed to Ali, not the Prophet ﷺ
Context suggests this is about Moses' sandals based on Quranic context

plainChains: معمر -> جابر بن يزيد -> عمير بن سعيد -> علي

potential_issues.issue: Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi (جابر بن يزيد الجعفي) is a weak narrator (Da'if) criticized by major hadith scholars
potential_issues.impact: Jabir al-Ju'fi is known for poor memory, confusion in narration, and Shi'i tendencies. Scholars like Yahya ibn Ma'in and others declared him weak. His presence in the chain significantly weakens the narration. However, he is not accused of lying (Kadhdhab), so this results in 'Weak But Might Be Acceptable' not 'Problematic'.

potential_issues.issue: This is a mawquf narration - a statement from Ali about Moses' sandals in context of Quranic interpretation
potential_issues.impact: The narration is Ali's tafsir commentary on the Quranic verse about Moses being commanded to remove his sandals. It is not a marfu' hadith from the Prophet ﷺ.

potential_issues.issue: Multiple uses of 'an (عَنْ) in the chain
potential_issues.impact: Combined with the weak narrator, the multiple 'an terms add to the chain's weakness.

Topics: Commentary on why Moses was commanded to remove sandals
Explanation that sandals were made from donkey skin
hadiths.arabicText: أرنا /94 مَعْمَرٌ /94 , عَنْ /26 جَابِرِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ /26 , عَنْ /26 عُمَيْرِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ /26 , /27 عَنْ /93 عَلِيٍّ L5722 /93 , قَالَ : /20 " كَانَتَا مِنْ جِلْدِ حِمَارٍ , فَقِيلَ لَهُ : اخْلَعْهُمَا " /27 *

hadiths.english_translation: Ibn al-Musayyib reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray it when he remembers it.' For indeed Allah says: 'And establish prayer for My remembrance' [Quran 20:14].

narrators.name: الزهري
narrators.full_name: محمد بن مسلم بن شهاب الزهري
reliabilityIssues: mudallis - Category 3 according to Ibn Hajar, but extremely reliable scholar

narrators.name: ابن المسيب
narrators.full_name: سعيد بن المسيب بن حزن المخزومي

chainIssues: Chain is mursal - Ibn al-Musayyib is a Tabi'i who did not meet the Prophet ﷺ (though he saw him as a very young child according to some reports)
Missing link between Ibn al-Musayyib and the Prophet ﷺ
Al-Zuhri uses 'an (عَنْ) and is classified as mudallis
No companion mentioned in the chain

plainChains: معمر -> الزهري -> ابن المسيب -> [DISCONNECTION] -> النبي ﷺ

potential_issues.issue: Al-Zuhri is classified as a mudallis (Category 3 per Ibn Hajar) and uses 'an (عَنْ)
potential_issues.impact: While Al-Zuhri's tadlis is noted, he is extremely reliable (Thiqah Thabt Hafiz). However, in a mursal narration, this adds another layer of ambiguity.

potential_issues.issue: Mursal narration - Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib is reporting directly from the Prophet ﷺ without mentioning an intermediary companion
potential_issues.impact: This is a mursal hadith. Ibn al-Musayyib is from the First Generation of Tabi'in and, although he saw the Prophet ﷺ as a very young child (around 8 years old at the Prophet's death), he did not reach the age to actively learn from him. There is a missing companion in the chain. Following grading rules, mursal narrations (disconnections) result in 'Weak But Might Be Acceptable' not 'Problematic'.

potential_issues.issue: Ibn al-Musayyib's mursal narrations are considered among the strongest mursal reports by scholars
potential_issues.impact: Despite being mursal, Ibn al-Musayyib's mursalat are given special consideration by hadith scholars due to his exceptional reliability and careful methodology. However, it remains mursal and thus disconnected.

Topics: Method of making up missed prayers
Obligation to pray when one remembers
Connection between Quranic verse and prophetic guidance
hadiths.arabicText: أرنا /94 مَعْمَرٌ L7633 /94 , عَنِ /26 الزُّهْرِيِّ L7272 /26 ، /27 عَنِ /26 ابْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ L3299 /26 ، أَنّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ : /20 " مَنْ نَسِيَ صَلاةً , فَلْيُصَلِّهَا إِذَا ذَكَرَهَا " ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقُولُ : /4 وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي سورة طه آية 14 /4 /27 *

hadiths.english_translation: Malik ibn Dinar said: 'It reached me (بَلَغَنِي) that the distance between the two jaws of Moses' staff when it became a snake was fifty cubits.'

chainIssues: Uses 'balaghanī' (بَلَغَنِي) which indicates receiving information without a direct chain
This creates a major disconnection - the source is unknown
No chain provided beyond Malik ibn Dinar
This is maqtu' - a statement from a Tabi'i without proper attribution

potential_issues.issue: Malik ibn Dinar uses the term 'balaghanī' (بَلَغَنِي - 'it reached me') which indicates indirect transmission without a known chain
potential_issues.impact: The use of 'balaghanī' creates a severe disconnection. The original source of this information is unknown, making it impossible to verify. This is similar to a mursal narration but even weaker since the intermediaries are completely unknown.

potential_issues.issue: Ja'far ibn Sulayman is Saduq with Shi'i tendencies
potential_issues.impact: While not weak enough to make the hadith 'Problematic', Ja'far's Shi'i leanings are noted. However, the main issue is the disconnection, not his grade.

potential_issues.issue: This appears to be an Israeli narration (Isra'iliyyat) about Prophet Moses
potential_issues.impact: Details about Moses' staff transforming into a snake with specific measurements are likely from Jewish or Christian sources rather than authentic Islamic transmission. Following grading rules, disconnections result in 'Weak But Might Be Acceptable'.

potential_issues.issue: The narration is maqtu' - Malik ibn Dinar's own report without proper chain
potential_issues.impact: This is not traced back to the Prophet ﷺ or even to a companion. It is a report from a Tabi' al-Tabi'i about an event from Moses' time, likely based on Isra'iliyyat.

Topics: Size of the snake that Moses' staff became
hadiths.arabicText: أرنا /94 جَعْفَرٌ /94 , /27 عَنْ /26 مَالِكِ بْنِ دِينَارٍ /26 , قَالَ : /20 " بَلَغَنِي أَنَّهُ كَانَ بَيْنَ لَحْيَيْ عَصَا مُوسَى حِينَ عَادَتْ حَيَّةً خَمْسُونَ ذِرَاعًا " /27 *
